source_caption:
Uma Thurman was completely omitted from Quentin Tarantino's original typed casting wishlist for Pulp Fiction. When the director's early casting sheets leaked online, they revealed that the iconic role of Mia Wallace was originally envisioned for other actresses. Tarantino's primary options for the character included Virginia Madsen, Alfre Woodard, Bridget Fonda, Angela Bassett, and Jennifer Beals.

Despite not being on the initial list, Uma Thurman was ultimately convinced to take the role of Mia Wallace after director Quentin Tarantino read her the script over the phone. Her hesitation stemmed from the screenplay's intense and controversial themes, but the character went on to become one of the most iconic roles of her career, earning her an Academy Award nomination for Best Supporting Actress.
